value.rationale: The Goldner–Harary graph is a uniquely natural smallest non-Hamiltonian maximal planar graph and a small planar 3-tree; its deterministic majority dynamics had no located exact basin treatment. The complete 2048-state classification reveals a substantive disparity: 47 persistent oscillatory attractors collectively attract only \(89/1024\) states, while just two consensus fixed points attract \(935/1024\), with 27 oscillating cycles isolated and a sharp four-round entrance cutoff. These are natural orbit and basin invariants directly measuring deterministic opinion stabilization; they are not implied by general eventual-period theory or random-network dynamics, and the exact symmetry decomposition supports comparison of planar network topologies.
